findings.summary: Published JWT signing-key fallback and optional tokenVersion still allow administrator impersonation when JWT_SECRET is absent. A forged token reached the admin users endpoint with HTTP 200.
Default demonstration administrator credentials still work under the audit profile; the initializer is enabled for every profile except the exact name prod.

Two case-variant email registrations created distinct user IDs. The second user read the first order and switched it to COD (both HTTP 200). Payment initiation uses the same unsafe ownership comparison.
Running the startup loader changed stock 0 to 45, inactive to active, and price 1 to 38,500. It now also overwrites cost price and lead time.
A concurrent description edit restored inventory consumed by a sale: 41 to 40 to 41. Product still has no optimistic version, and the edit does not share checkout locking.
Two pending orders using a promotion limited to one use both confirmed through COD. The usage check excludes pending reservations and is not repeated at finalization.
The API accepted a 150% promotion and created an order totaling LKR -19,050. Percentage validation and a final nonnegative-total invariant remain missing.
Legacy checkout without shipping information committed an order and returned HTTP 200 with invalid JSON. Entity recursion and duplicate-retry risk remain.
A correctly signed simulated chargeback following success returned 200 and left the payment SUCCESS. The terminal-state return still ignores -3.

Empty data now returns zero and demo mode is explicit. However, a single 10:00 sale still produces fabricated 35%/40%/25% morning/afternoon/evening profit buckets. Missing cost data is silently estimated. Original severity reduced from High; see F41, F42 and F44.
Missing database settings still select volatile H2 and automatic schema update, including production-like profiles. No fail-fast persistent-database requirement exists.

Bootstrap SQL still requires obsolete order_items/cart_items fields that the entities do not write. The checkout migration excludes SHIPPED, DELIVERED and legacy PAID/PENDING values used by current code/seeds. Fresh PostgreSQL installation and upgrade remain unverified.
Recovery still sends INITIATED payments to a helper that acts only on REFUND_PENDING. Started payments are excluded from expiry; no provider retrieval or merchant review path resolves uncertainty.
The alternate create-admin endpoint still promotes without the acting administrator password. The reauthentication check is conditional on the password being supplied.
Login still trusts the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For value. Counters use separate get/put operations, clear partial counts wholesale, and are process-local.

Receipt upload accepts arbitrary content/extensions and stores a new UUID file on every replacement. Downloads still use the generic static uploads handler with no order-owner check; no aggregate quota or replacement cleanup exists.

A newly registered, unverified mailbox immediately became subscribed. Delivery is disabled by default, but enabling marketing makes these accounts eligible without mailbox confirmation. No mail was sent during this check.
Two synchronized administrator deactivations both completed without error, leaving zero active administrators. The count-then-write check does not serialize the invariant.

Qualifying status filters now exclude pending, failed, cancelled and refunded orders. The fixture with sales 100, cost 40 and discount 20 reports netProfit 40. Revenue is defined as gross sales; this does not establish collected cash or resolve the other analytics findings.
latest?limit=1000000 still returns the entire 25-product catalog; latest/featured lack a safe maximum before query creation and multiplication.

Chat now caches catalog reads for 60 seconds and limits message length, but caches entities unsafely (F38). Autocomplete still reads all active products and performs unbounded edit-distance work for each request; chat FAQs still fill the catalog cache.
A public page containing ten products executed 46 prepared database statements. Full entity serialization still loads lazy collections individually.

Analytics now filters bounded date ranges in SQL and fetches order items, an improvement. Order history remains unpaged; the dashboard loads all users to count them; all-time analytics and public trending recommendations still load full order histories.

Audience preparation still loops across all subscribers, catalog candidates and full purchase histories inside a global queue transaction. It runs even with delivery disabled. Dashboard counts remain one query per campaign/status.
The global cart provider still replaces all routes while account/cart loading is pending. API requests have no timeout, so a stalled request can prevent even the storefront or login screen rendering.
Password changes invalidate the server token, but ChangePasswordForm supplies no completion handler and Axios has no centralized 401 handling. The UI remains signed in with revoked credentials.

AuthContext still does not observe cross-tab token changes while Axios reads the shared token on each request. A tab can display one identity and send another identity's credentials; skipped cart saves can remain in syncing state.
Autocomplete and administrator search still accept out-of-order responses. There is no cancellation or sequence guard, and administrator search is not debounced.
The backend inventory rules permit INVENTORY_MANAGER but the management UI and dashboard method security remain ADMIN-only. Intended inventory duties cannot be completed through the UI.
Security CORS origins are still hardcoded to localhost and ignore FRONTEND_URL. A separately hosted frontend remains blocked unless a same-origin proxy or other deployment override compensates.
Every route is still eagerly imported. The measured main bundle is 1,216.77 kB (339.81 kB gzip), larger than the earlier 1,155.71 kB. See the installed-package/lockfile limitation below.
The default hero remains 1,988,419 bytes without responsive variants. Metadata hydrates the image blob, and the versioned image endpoint still returns no-cache without an explicit validator.

CSV escaping still only quotes text and escapes quotation marks. Formula-leading product/category names remain executable spreadsheet formulas when opened by a spreadsheet application. No spreadsheet exploit was run.

The saved npm lockfile still reports 14 affected packages. A fresh query of 131 backend coordinates reports 8 matching packages and 22 unique advisory IDs. These are advisory matches, not 22 confirmed exploits.
Lint now reports 23 errors and 6 warnings. CI still builds without enforcing lint and uses a fixed backend startup sleep; existing passing tests miss the reproduced failures.

The example PostgreSQL URL still uses sslmode=require and channel_binding instead of the JDBC property channelBinding. Encryption alone does not authenticate the database server; live connection settings were not inspected.

Normal startup creates historical demonstration sales
Cost and supplier lead-time updates silently do nothing
Delivered purchases no longer qualify for product reviews
